precepts.text: They that are whole have no need of the physician; I came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.
precepts.why:
Christ is the physician: “When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick”. If you think you're good, that you know everything, you don't need the son of God, you don't need the Saviour.

You have to admit you're sick: that we are in the midst of sin, and that all we have done has been wrong. That is the same thing as accepting the punishment of our iniquity.

“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” He did not call us righteous. He came for sinners. That is the healing Jeremiah promises Israel, whose “sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity”. The sick nation is the one he came to heal.

The churches are the opposite: they say they don't need that Bible, they are already whole. Isaiah 65 shows them saying so, “I am holier than thou.” The ones who think themselves whole will not come to the physician.

precepts.text: The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath; therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
precepts.point: Christians use Mark 2:27 to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
Christians use this verse to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. “The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.”

The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel. Man was not put on the earth for the sabbath; the sabbath was put on the earth for man. And the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it: “in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed.” He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude, “a perpetual covenant” and “a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever”.

precepts.text: The Pharisees challenged Christ's disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, saying it was not lawful.
precepts.point: Link this history with the words of Christ: when the Pharisees challenged his disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, Christ recounted this very history of David and the shewbread. Precept this in your bibles if you do not have it already.

note.label: 1 Samuel 21: The Hallowed Bread and the Feigned Madness

precepts.why:
Christ “went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn. And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?”

When the Pharisees challenged his disciples, Christ recounted this very history of David and the shewbread. Link this history with the words of Christ, and precept it in your bibles if you do not have it already.

note.label: 1 Samuel 21: The Hallowed Bread and the Feigned Madness

precepts.why:
Christ answered, “Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him? How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?”

This is that history. In Nob, “the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before the Lord.” David had been out in the field three days, fearful of king Saul, when he came to Nob in need.

points: It can manifest as indifference and apathy, or a dismissive demeanour. While temporary feelings of indifference are common, a persistent I don't care attitude can have negative consequences for relationships and personal growth. You see that? That I don't care attitude provides a negative consequence on personal growth. You cannot continue to grow and get better in the truth if you have got an I don't care attitude. So we have got to kill that old man, or that old woman, that does not want to change. We have got to be able to change.
No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment. Meaning, look, you cannot serve God and become newness in spirit with that old man or that old woman. You have got to let it go.

Else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse. That new piece is going to take away from the old, or that old piece is going to spring up in the new man or the new woman. We cannot have it.
And no man putteth new wine into old bottles. You cannot put new wine into an old bottle. You have to change. You have to change dramatically in order to grow, to go to the next levels in the truth.

Else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles. You see that? When you repent, you must be spiritually changed completely. And you have to counsel and take advice from people with more experience than you.
